summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 30%), atrial fibrillation, restrictive lung disease, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and chest pressure over two days, associated with URI symptoms. Initial evaluation revealed acute on chronic kidney injury (creatinine 2.2, baseline 1.5), likely prerenal from mild heart failure, and elevated BNP of 650. He was treated with nebulizers and a short course of prednisone for reactive airway disease in the setting of a viral upper respiratory infection. Antibiotics were discontinued after clarification that he does not have COPD. His kidney function initially improved with diuresis but worsened to 2.7 due to over-diuresis; it subsequently improved to 2.3 with holding torsemide and IV fluids. He was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to follow up with his PCP for labs and medication management, pulmonology for ongoing lung evaluation, and a scheduled CT for a known pulmonary nodule. Amiodarone was continued, but concern for its pulmonary effects was communicated to cardiology.
